Question: How do you combine simple returns from consecutive periods?
Answer: Multiply their gross return factors, then subtract one.
Explanation: A rise from 100 to 125 and a fall back to 100 give gross factors of 1.25 and 0.80. Their product is 1, so the cumulative return is zero.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, financial data and returns — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: How is marked equity computed for a cash account holding a single stock?
Answer: Cash plus shares held times the current mark.
Explanation: The $480 cash balance and $520 market value of stock are both assets. With no debt, together they give $1,000 of equity.
Source: Boyd et al., Multi-Period Trading via Convex Optimization, portfolio dynamics and cash account — https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/cvx_portfolio.html

Question: When a short seller buys shares to return them to the lender, what happens to share inventory?
Answer: The negative share balance moves toward zero.
Explanation: Each $2 rise costs this short position $100. Buying back some of the 50 borrowed shares would reduce the loss from the next rise.
Source: NYU Tandon, Practical Introduction to Quantitative Equity Trading, lecture 1, short sales and P&L — https://engineering.nyu.edu/sites/default/files/2020-07/Practical-Inroduction-to-Quantitative-Trading-baver.pdf

Question: What converts a futures price change in points to dollar P&L on one long contract?
Answer: Multiply by the contract's dollar value per point.
Explanation: Each point in contract B is worth $10 per contract. Three contracts therefore gain or lose $30 per point, even though their notional at 200 points is $6,000.
Source: CME Group, Introduction to Futures, contract specifications, tick movements and margin — https://www.cmegroup.com/education/courses/introduction-to-futures

Question: With the FX quote in home currency per foreign unit, how do you translate a foreign asset value?
Answer: Multiply local value by the exchange rate.
Explanation: The asset stays at 80 local units. At $1.25 per unit it is worth $100, and at $1.10 it is worth $88.
Source: OpenStax, Principles of Finance, exchange rates and international finance — https://openstax.org/details/books/principles-finance

Question: For an option-free fixed bond, what happens to its present value when all discount rates rise?
Answer: It falls because the same cash flows are discounted more heavily.
Explanation: With the promised payments fixed, raising the yield from 2% to 4% lowers the price from 90.57 to 82.19.
Source: CME Group, Calculating the Dollar Value of a Basis Point, price sensitivity and dollar value of a basis point — https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/interest-rates/calculating-the-dollar-value-of-a-basis-point.html

Question: How do you obtain a long call's expiry profit from its intrinsic value?
Answer: Subtract the premium paid.
Explanation: At a stock price of $55, a $50 call pays $5. Deducting the $3 premium leaves $2 profit per share.
Source: Options Industry Council, Option Price Behavior, intrinsic value and premiums — https://www.optionseducation.org/referencelibrary/faq/option-price-behavior

Question: Who typically transacts directly with an ETF in large creation units?
Answer: An authorized participant.
Explanation: An authorized participant can buy the basket and create ETF shares. Spending $50.35 per share after costs to sell at $50.30 would lose five cents.
Source: SEC, Updated Investor Bulletin on ETFs, creation, redemption and secondary-market prices — https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins-24

Question: With positive perpetual funding paid by longs, which side receives the payment?
Answer: Shorts holding through the funding timestamp.
Explanation: For a $100,000 long, each basis point of positive funding costs $10. The three signed rates sum to +4 bp, a net $40 payment to shorts.
Source: Coinbase, Understanding Funding Rates in Perpetual Futures, funding payments and contract mechanics — https://www.coinbase.com/learn/perpetual-futures/understanding-funding-rates-in-perpetual-futures

Question: A position gains 20% and then loses 20%. What is its cumulative simple return?
Explanation: 1.2 × 0.8 − 1 = −0.04. Worked example — From $100, a 20% gain makes $120. A 20% loss on $120 ends at $96.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, financial data and returns — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: Buying 10 shares at $30 with a $2 commission requires what cash debit?
Explanation: The fee reduces cash at the fill.
Source: Boyd et al., Multi-Period Trading via Convex Optimization, portfolio dynamics and cash account — https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/cvx_portfolio.html

Question: A trader shorts 100 shares at $30, covers at $27 and pays $40 total fees. What is net profit?
Explanation: 100 × (30 − 27) − 40. Worked example — Selling then buying back 100 shares at a $3 difference yields $300 gross. Fees leave $260.
Source: NYU Tandon, Practical Introduction to Quantitative Equity Trading, lecture 1, short sales and P&L — https://engineering.nyu.edu/sites/default/files/2020-07/Practical-Inroduction-to-Quantitative-Trading-baver.pdf

Question: Three long futures with a $50 multiplier drop 2 points. What daily variation margin cash flow follows?
Explanation: 3 × 50 × (−2). Worked example — Three $50-per-point contracts gain or lose $150 for each point. A two-point fall costs $300.
Source: CME Group, Introduction to Futures, contract specifications, tick movements and margin — https://www.cmegroup.com/education/courses/introduction-to-futures

Question: A stock gains 10% locally and its currency falls 5% in home terms. What home-currency return results?
Explanation: 1.10 × 0.95 − 1. Worked example — Start at 100. The asset grows to 110 in local terms. Converting at a 5% weaker currency leaves 104.5 in initial home units.
Source: OpenStax, Principles of Finance, exchange rates and international finance — https://openstax.org/details/books/principles-finance

Question: A portfolio has modified duration 4. What is the approximate percentage price change for a parallel +25 bp yield shock?
Explanation: −4 × 0.0025 = −0.01. Worked example — A modified duration of four gives about a 1% price decline for a 0.25 percentage point yield rise.
Source: CME Group, Calculating the Dollar Value of a Basis Point, price sensitivity and dollar value of a basis point — https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/interest-rates/calculating-the-dollar-value-of-a-basis-point.html

Question: A long put struck at $50 costs $3 and expires with stock at $42. What is profit per share?
Explanation: 8 intrinsic minus 3 premium. Worked example — The $50 put costs $3. At $42 the difference between payoff and net profit is still $3.
Source: Options Industry Council, Option Price Behavior, intrinsic value and premiums — https://www.optionseducation.org/referencelibrary/faq/option-price-behavior

Question: An ETF trades at $101 against a tradable $100 creation basket. Before costs, which side of the trade sells the rich asset?
Answer: Sell the ETF shares.
Source: SEC, Updated Investor Bulletin on ETFs, creation, redemption and secondary-market prices — https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins-24

Question: A $40,000 long pays one 0.02% funding interval. What is its cash flow?
Source: Coinbase, Understanding Funding Rates in Perpetual Futures, funding payments and contract mechanics — https://www.coinbase.com/learn/perpetual-futures/understanding-funding-rates-in-perpetual-futures

Question: A researcher adds daily log returns and reports the sum as a simple return. What final conversion is missing?
Answer: Exponentiate the sum and subtract one.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, financial data and returns — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: A backtest records sale proceeds and also credits the whole sale value as profit. What was counted twice?
Answer: The value of the disposed inventory.
Explanation: Realized profit depends on the cost basis.
Source: Boyd et al., Multi-Period Trading via Convex Optimization, portfolio dynamics and cash account — https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/cvx_portfolio.html

Question: A short backtest lets every candidate enter even when no borrow is available. Which simulated quantity is overstated?
Answer: The set of executable short positions.
Source: NYU Tandon, Practical Introduction to Quantitative Equity Trading, lecture 1, short sales and P&L — https://engineering.nyu.edu/sites/default/files/2020-07/Practical-Inroduction-to-Quantitative-Trading-baver.pdf

Question: Why is posted initial margin a poor denominator for comparing the market exposure of two futures strategies?
Answer: Margin is collateral; exposure depends on contract notional.
Source: CME Group, Introduction to Futures, contract specifications, tick movements and margin — https://www.cmegroup.com/education/courses/introduction-to-futures

Question: A USD investor owes a fixed EUR invoice. Which move in USD per EUR increases the USD liability?
Answer: An increase in USD per EUR.
Source: OpenStax, Principles of Finance, exchange rates and international finance — https://openstax.org/details/books/principles-finance

Question: Why does a first-order duration estimate deteriorate for a large yield shock?
Answer: It omits the curvature of the price–yield relationship.
Source: CME Group, Calculating the Dollar Value of a Basis Point, price sensitivity and dollar value of a basis point — https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/interest-rates/calculating-the-dollar-value-of-a-basis-point.html

Question: An option buyer loses money despite a positive intrinsic value at expiry. What cost can explain it?
Answer: The premium exceeded intrinsic value.
Source: Options Industry Council, Option Price Behavior, intrinsic value and premiums — https://www.optionseducation.org/referencelibrary/faq/option-price-behavior

Question: An overseas ETF shows a premium to yesterday's NAV while its component market is closed. What should be checked before declaring arbitrage?
Answer: Whether the basket valuation is current and executable.
Source: SEC, Updated Investor Bulletin on ETFs, creation, redemption and secondary-market prices — https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins-24

Question: A spot-long, perpetual-short basis trade has nearly flat delta. Why might the short leg still be liquidated?
Answer: Collateral at its venue may be insufficient during an adverse move.
Source: Coinbase, Understanding Funding Rates in Perpetual Futures, funding payments and contract mechanics — https://www.coinbase.com/learn/perpetual-futures/understanding-funding-rates-in-perpetual-futures

Question: What loss from the first close takes this account back to its starting value?
Explanation: The fall is 25 on a base of 125.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, financial data and returns — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: What is the marked equity of this debt-free account?
Explanation: The inventory contributes its current market value.
Source: Boyd et al., Multi-Period Trading via Convex Optimization, portfolio dynamics and cash account — https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/cvx_portfolio.html

Question: Using the slope of this short-position P&L, how many shares are short?
Answer: 50 shares.
Explanation: A $2 rise costs $100.
Source: NYU Tandon, Practical Introduction to Quantitative Equity Trading, lecture 1, short sales and P&L — https://engineering.nyu.edu/sites/default/files/2020-07/Practical-Inroduction-to-Quantitative-Trading-baver.pdf

Question: Index B trades at 200 points with a $10 multiplier. What gross notional does the plotted B position represent?
Source: CME Group, Introduction to Futures, contract specifications, tick movements and margin — https://www.cmegroup.com/education/courses/introduction-to-futures

Question: A foreign asset stays at 80 local units over this chart. What dollar P&L does one unit of the asset generate?
Source: OpenStax, Principles of Finance, exchange rates and international finance — https://openstax.org/details/books/principles-finance

Question: Which two-percentage-point yield increase produces the larger dollar price drop in the chart?
Explanation: About 8.38 points versus 7.46.
Source: CME Group, Calculating the Dollar Value of a Basis Point, price sensitivity and dollar value of a basis point — https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/interest-rates/calculating-the-dollar-value-of-a-basis-point.html

Question: At what underlying price does this call break even?
Explanation: Above the $50 strike, each additional dollar adds one dollar of profit.
Source: Options Industry Council, Option Price Behavior, intrinsic value and premiums — https://www.optionseducation.org/referencelibrary/faq/option-price-behavior

Question: After all costs, what spread remains from creating shares and selling at the displayed ETF bid?
Answer: −$0.05 per share.
Source: SEC, Updated Investor Bulletin on ETFs, creation, redemption and secondary-market prices — https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins-24

Question: A constant $100,000 perpetual long spans all three settlements. What is its total funding cash flow?
Explanation: The net rate paid is 4 bp.
Source: Coinbase, Understanding Funding Rates in Perpetual Futures, funding payments and contract mechanics — https://www.coinbase.com/learn/perpetual-futures/understanding-funding-rates-in-perpetual-futures

Question: Which timestamp controls eligibility when joining an economic release to a trading signal?
Answer: When that version became available to the strategy.
Explanation: The April 5 release reported 1.2%. The revised May figure could only enter decisions after its release.
Source: St. Louis Fed, FRED API real-time periods, real-time periods and revised observations — https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/realtime_period.html

Question: What membership list belongs in a historical index-constituent strategy?
Answer: The constituents known to be eligible at each historical decision date.
Explanation: B belonged to the 2020 universe. Reconstructing that year from the 2022 list would omit a stock the strategy could actually have held.
Source: QuantConnect, Research Guide, survivorship bias and universe selection — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/key-concepts/research-guide

Question: What offsets the mechanical per-share price drop in a two-for-one split?
Answer: The share count doubles.
Explanation: Thirty shares at $80 become sixty at $40 after the two-for-one split. The holding is worth $2,400 on both sides of the split.
Source: QuantConnect, US Equity data handling, price normalization and corporate actions — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/securities/asset-classes/us-equity/handling-data

Question: Why map a continuous futures signal back to a dated contract before simulating fills?
Answer: The continuous series is synthetic and has no executable order book.
Explanation: The near contract stays at $98 and the deferred contract stays at $101. Switching which contract supplies the series introduces a $3 step despite unchanged quotes.
Source: QuantConnect, US Futures Security Master, contract mapping and price scaling — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/datasets/quantconnect/us-futures-security-master

Question: Why distinguish exchange event time from local receipt time in replay?
Answer: Receipt time determines when the strategy could act on that event.
Explanation: The exchange recorded the trade at 15 ms. Its local arrival at 28 ms came eight milliseconds after the decision.
Source: QuantConnect, Reality Modeling, time modeling, time zones and market hours — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/key-concepts

Question: What does a forward-filled price establish about tradability during the gap?
Answer: Only the last known value; it establishes no current executable liquidity.
Explanation: Quote B is 80 seconds old. Under a ten-second age limit, its last price is historical information and cannot establish current executable size.
Source: QuantConnect, Reality Modeling, data handling and fill-forward — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/key-concepts

Question: When is a full interval's high available to a close-of-bar strategy?
Answer: After all eligible trades through the end of that interval have arrived.
Explanation: Path B trades down to 8 before rising to 12. Path A visits 12 first. A completed OHLC bar summarizes either path and loses that ordering.
Source: QuantConnect, Reality Modeling, time periods and consolidating data — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/key-concepts

Question: Which identifier should link trades across a ticker change?
Answer: A persistent instrument identifier with effective-dated ticker mappings.
Explanation: Ticker Q referred to listing 12 in 2019. The effective dates select the security associated with a historical trade.
Source: QuantConnect, Research Guide, data quality and reproducible research — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/key-concepts/research-guide

Question: January employment is published February 7 and revised March 7. Which value may a February 20 backtest use?
Answer: The February 7 release.
Source: St. Louis Fed, FRED API real-time periods, real-time periods and revised observations — https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/realtime_period.html

Question: A stock disappears between rebalances in bankruptcy. What terminal observation must a return backtest seek?
Answer: Its delisting return or actual recovery.
Source: QuantConnect, Research Guide, survivorship bias and universe selection — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/key-concepts/research-guide

Question: A stock closes at $50 then at $49 ex a $1 cash dividend. What is its one-day total return before costs?
Explanation: (49 + 1) / 50 − 1. Worked example — At the ex-date the share is worth $49 and the dividend is $1. The total equals the initial $50.
Source: QuantConnect, US Equity data handling, price normalization and corporate actions — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/securities/asset-classes/us-equity/handling-data

Question: A strategy rolls one long near contract into one deferred contract. What quantity must the ledger track separately for each expiry?
Answer: Its actual fills and marked position.
Source: QuantConnect, US Futures Security Master, contract mapping and price scaling — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/datasets/quantconnect/us-futures-security-master

Question: Two venues close at 16:00 local in different time zones. What must happen before joining their closes?
Answer: Convert to a common timeline with the applicable session calendars.
Source: QuantConnect, Reality Modeling, time modeling, time zones and market hours — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/key-concepts

Question: A halted stock has a repeated mark for an hour. What should the simulator do with attempted market buys during the halt?
Answer: Keep them unfilled or model the venue's actual rejection or queuing policy.
Source: QuantConnect, Reality Modeling, data handling and fill-forward — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/key-concepts

Question: A bar hits both a stop and a target. What extra evidence determines which filled first?
Answer: Intrabar event order and executable liquidity.
Source: QuantConnect, Reality Modeling, time periods and consolidating data — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/key-concepts

Question: A vendor restates a historical price. What should a researcher retain to reproduce the original run?
Answer: The exact input snapshot or a retrievable version identified by its hash.
Source: QuantConnect, Research Guide, data quality and reproducible research — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/key-concepts/research-guide

Question: A macro model loses its edge when switched from latest data to historical vintages. What bias did latest data permit?
Answer: Look-ahead through revisions.
Source: St. Louis Fed, FRED API real-time periods, real-time periods and revised observations — https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/realtime_period.html

Question: An analyst deletes every name without a complete ten-year history. What selection effect follows?
Answer: The sample conditions on survival and continued data availability.
Source: QuantConnect, Research Guide, survivorship bias and universe selection — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/key-concepts/research-guide

Question: A simulation uses dividend-adjusted total returns and credits dividends to cash again. Which result is biased upward?
Answer: Portfolio total return.
Source: QuantConnect, US Equity data handling, price normalization and corporate actions — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/securities/asset-classes/us-equity/handling-data

Question: A concatenated contract chart jumps on a roll while both contracts are unchanged. What created the jump?
Answer: Switching between differently priced maturities.
Source: QuantConnect, US Futures Security Master, contract mapping and price scaling — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/datasets/quantconnect/us-futures-security-master

Question: A daily signal uses the overseas close that occurs two hours after the local order. What dependency is invalid?
Answer: The signal depends on a future observation.
Source: QuantConnect, Reality Modeling, time modeling, time zones and market hours — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/key-concepts

Question: Replacing a missing return with zero reduces estimated volatility. Which assumption caused the reduction?
Answer: Missing observations were treated as observed zero changes.
Source: QuantConnect, Reality Modeling, data handling and fill-forward — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/key-concepts

Question: What happens to elapsed clock time per fixed-volume bar when trading activity accelerates?
Answer: It usually decreases.
Source: QuantConnect, Reality Modeling, time periods and consolidating data — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/key-concepts

Question: Two different companies use the same ticker years apart. What goes wrong in an unqualified ticker join?
Answer: Their histories can be stitched into a fictitious security.
Source: QuantConnect, Research Guide, data quality and reproducible research — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/key-concepts/research-guide

Question: At an April 30 decision, what value of this observation is eligible?
Explanation: Only the first release was public.
Source: St. Louis Fed, FRED API real-time periods, real-time periods and revised observations — https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/realtime_period.html

Question: Using 1 for membership, which eligible 2020 name disappears if you use only the 2022 list?
Answer: B.
Explanation: B was a member in 2020 and absent in 2022.
Source: QuantConnect, Research Guide, survivorship bias and universe selection — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/key-concepts/research-guide

Question: If this change is entirely a two-for-one split, how many post-split shares replace 30 pre-split shares?
Answer: 60 shares.
Explanation: The holding still has $2,400 of value.
Source: QuantConnect, US Equity data handling, price normalization and corporate actions — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/securities/asset-classes/us-equity/handling-data

Question: A raw series uses near on Monday and deferred on Tuesday. How much of its +$3 change reflects within-contract price movement?
Explanation: Both underlying quotes were unchanged.
Source: QuantConnect, US Futures Security Master, contract mapping and price scaling — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/datasets/quantconnect/us-futures-security-master

Question: How many milliseconds after this decision did the trade first become usable locally?
Answer: 8 ms.
Source: QuantConnect, Reality Modeling, time modeling, time zones and market hours — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/key-concepts

Question: Under a rule rejecting quotes older than ten seconds, which symbol is ineligible?
Answer: B.
Explanation: Its quote age is 80 seconds.
Source: QuantConnect, Reality Modeling, data handling and fill-forward — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/key-concepts

Question: Both paths have the same OHLC. With an active sell stop at 9 and sell target at 12, which path reaches the stop first, before the target?
Answer: Path B.
Explanation: Its second trade drops to 8.
Source: QuantConnect, Reality Modeling, time periods and consolidating data — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/key-concepts

Question: Both listings used ticker Q. Which permanent ID belongs to a Q trade in 2019?
Answer: ID 12.
Explanation: Only that listing was active in 2019.
Source: QuantConnect, Research Guide, data quality and reproducible research — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/key-concepts/research-guide

Question: How do you compute expected trade P&L from discrete outcomes?
Answer: Sum each outcome multiplied by its probability.
Explanation: Across 100 trades, the losing group contributes −$100 and the two winning groups contribute $30 and $100. Dividing the $30 total by 100 gives $0.30 per trade.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, expected return and return distributions — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: For n independent equal-variance returns, how does standard error of the mean scale with n?
Answer: It declines in proportion to 1/√n.
Explanation: Quadrupling the independent sample from 100 to 400 lowers the standard error from 4 bp to 2 bp.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, parameter estimation and sample moments — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: What does a market-model residual measure on a given day?
Answer: Actual return minus the return fitted from the market model.
Explanation: Across a four-point change in market return, the fitted stock return changes by six points. That slope of 1.5 sets the market contribution used to calculate a residual.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, time series regression and fitted values — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: How do you convert the covariance of two returns to their correlation?
Answer: Divide by the product of their standard deviations.
Explanation: The diagonal entries give volatilities of 0.20 and 0.10 after taking square roots. Dividing the off-diagonal covariance of 0.01 by their product gives correlation 0.5.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, covariance matrices and portfolio variance — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: Which moments must stay time-invariant for weak stationarity?
Answer: A constant finite mean and autocovariance depending only on lag.
Explanation: The level rises from 101 to 104 between dates 3 and 4, giving a first difference of +3. Stationarity of a differenced series is assessed across observations.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, stationarity and differencing — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: In a stationary AR(1), how does an initial deviation from the mean propagate k steps in expectation?
Answer: Multiply it by the autoregressive coefficient raised to k.
Explanation: With an autoregressive coefficient of 0.5, an expected deviation of 16 falls to 8 after one step and 4 after two.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, autoregressive models — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: For two I(1) prices, what defines cointegration?
Answer: Some nonzero linear combination is stationary.
Explanation: Subtracting twice B from A leaves 1 at each of the four dates. This illustrates a candidate spread. Four observations alone cannot establish stationarity.
Source: Engle & Granger, Co-integration and Error Correction, equilibrium errors and error correction — https://doi.org/10.2307/1913236

Question: In GARCH(1,1), which previous observation supplies the news term in the variance update?
Answer: The previous squared innovation.
Explanation: Day 2 has an innovation of −4. Squaring it gives 16, the largest news input to the variance update in this sample.
Source: Engle, Risk and Volatility, conditional heteroskedasticity and volatility forecasting — https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/06/engle-lecture.pdf

Question: Why sample contiguous blocks of returns instead of individual days?
Answer: To retain short-range serial dependence within sampled blocks.
Explanation: Resample A copies days 4–6 as one block and days 1–3 as another. Each block retains the original ordering of neighboring returns.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, bootstrapping and time series — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: In a market model with an intercept, what is the fitted excess return when market excess return is zero?
Answer: The intercept.
Explanation: The beta-times-market term is zero.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, time series regression and fitted values — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: In a return covariance matrix, what does the diagonal entry for stock B measure?
Answer: B’s return variance.
Explanation: Its square root gives B’s volatility over the same return horizon.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, covariance matrices and portfolio variance — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: For a candidate spread A − hB, which coefficient sets the number of B units per unit of A?
Answer: h, the hedge ratio.
Explanation: Using it defines a spread whose stability can then be tested.
Source: Engle & Granger, Co-integration and Error Correction, equilibrium errors and error correction — https://doi.org/10.2307/1913236

Question: In a symmetric GARCH variance update, which has the larger news term, a +3 or −3 return shock of the same units?
Answer: They have equal news terms.
Explanation: Squaring removes the sign.
Source: Engle, Risk and Volatility, conditional heteroskedasticity and volatility forecasting — https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/06/engle-lecture.pdf

Question: A moving-block bootstrap draws a block starting on day 7 with length 3. What is the last day of this block?
Answer: Day 9.
Explanation: The block contains days 7, 8 and 9.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, bootstrapping and time series — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: At the final close, what is the residual in percentage points?
Answer: −1 percentage point.
Explanation: Observed 2% minus fitted 3% equals −1 percentage point.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, time series regression and fitted values — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: The plotted returns are centered on their respective means. What sign will their covariance have?
Answer: Negative.
Explanation: Positive deviations in A occur with negative deviations in B, and vice versa.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, covariance matrices and portfolio variance — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: Use one unit of each asset. On which date is A − B furthest above its starting level?
Answer: Date 3.
Explanation: The spreads are 2, 2, 5 and 2.
Source: Engle & Granger, Co-integration and Error Correction, equilibrium errors and error correction — https://doi.org/10.2307/1913236

Question: The news term equals 0.25 times the squared shock. What does session B contribute?
Answer: 1 variance unit.
Explanation: Session B has shock −2. Its squared shock is 4.
Source: Engle, Risk and Volatility, conditional heteroskedasticity and volatility forecasting — https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/06/engle-lecture.pdf

Question: This resample uses consecutive blocks of length three. Across which adjacent output positions is there a splice?
Answer: Positions 3 and 4.
Explanation: The resample jumps from source day 6 to day 2 there.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, bootstrapping and time series — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: A stock has beta −0.5. What market-linked move does the model predict when market excess return falls 2%?
Answer: A gain of 1 percentage point.
Explanation: The two negative signs give a positive contribution before adding the intercept.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, time series regression and fitted values — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: If one return series is constant throughout the sample, what happens to its Pearson correlation with another asset?
Answer: It is undefined.
Explanation: The denominator includes a zero standard deviation.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, covariance matrices and portfolio variance — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: A spread has been stationary around $4. What equilibrium level should its forecast revert toward under that model?
Explanation: A stationary spread can have a nonzero mean.
Source: Engle & Granger, Co-integration and Error Correction, equilibrium errors and error correction — https://doi.org/10.2307/1913236

Question: If yesterday’s conditional variance is 2 and its GARCH persistence coefficient is 0.8, how much variance is carried forward?
Answer: 1.6 variance units.
Explanation: Multiply the old variance by its coefficient.
Source: Engle, Risk and Volatility, conditional heteroskedasticity and volatility forecasting — https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/06/engle-lecture.pdf

Question: A bootstrap draws blocks with replacement. Can the same source block legitimately appear twice in one resample?
Answer: Yes, it can be drawn again.
Explanation: Repeated blocks represent sampling variation.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, bootstrapping and time series — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: A trade wins $1 with 80% probability and loses $6 otherwise. What is its expectancy before fees?
Explanation: 0.8 × 1 − 0.2 × 6. Worked example — Frequent wins contribute $0.80. Infrequent losses contribute −$1.20. Net expectancy is −$0.40.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, expected return and return distributions — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: Independent daily returns have standard deviation 2%. With 100 observations what is the estimated standard error of the mean?
Answer: 0.2 percentage points.
Explanation: Worked example — With 2% outcome volatility the uncertainty of the mean is 2% divided by the square root of the observation count.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, parameter estimation and sample moments — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: A fitted market model has a +0.1% intercept. Today the beta-times-market term is +3%. What is fitted excess return?
Explanation: Worked example — A 0.1% intercept plus 1.5 times a 2% market return gives a fitted 3.1%.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, time series regression and fitted values — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: Two returns have covariance 0.006 and a product of standard deviations of 0.020 in matching units. What is their correlation?
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, covariance matrices and portfolio variance — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: A price follows a random walk with IID zero-mean innovations. Which one-period transformation recovers its stationary innovation series?
Answer: First differences.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, stationarity and differencing — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: With coefficient 0.5, a current deviation of 8 has what expected deviation two steps ahead?
Explanation: 8 × 0.5². Worked example — The expected offset falls from 8 to 4 to 2 under persistence 0.5.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, autoregressive models — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: A fitted spread is A − 2B. How many units of B offset one long unit of A in that spread?
Answer: Short two B units.
Source: Engle & Granger, Co-integration and Error Correction, equilibrium errors and error correction — https://doi.org/10.2307/1913236

Question: In a GARCH update, yesterday’s variance contributes 0.7, the squared shock contributes 0.8 and the constant is 0.1. What is the new variance?
Answer: 1.6 variance units.
Explanation: Worked example — The intercept, shock and persistence contribute 0.1, 0.8 and 0.7 respectively.
Source: Engle, Risk and Volatility, conditional heteroskedasticity and volatility forecasting — https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/06/engle-lecture.pdf

Question: What does a time-series bootstrap with one-observation blocks reduce to when blocks are sampled uniformly with replacement?
Answer: An ordinary IID resample of individual observations.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, bootstrapping and time series — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: Why can a higher hit rate coincide with a lower expected return?
Answer: Losses may grow in size relative to wins.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, expected return and return distributions — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: Why can an IID standard error be too small for positively autocorrelated strategy returns?
Answer: Adjacent returns contain overlapping information.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, parameter estimation and sample moments — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: A fitted intercept is positive but highly uncertain. What inference about persistent alpha remains unsupported?
Answer: That the underlying intercept is positive out of sample.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, time series regression and fitted values — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: Why does covariance change when one return series is converted from decimals to percent while correlation stays the same?
Answer: Covariance carries units; positive rescaling cancels in correlation.
Explanation: Worked example — Multiplying one axis by 100 stretches its numerical scale and covariance. Positive rescaling leaves correlation unchanged.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, covariance matrices and portfolio variance — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: Two unrelated trending price levels have high regression R². What time-series problem should be checked first?
Answer: Spurious regression caused by nonstationary levels.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, stationarity and differencing — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: A fitted AR coefficient is 1.02. Why is a stationary mean-reversion half-life inappropriate?
Answer: Deviations grow in expectation under that fitted model.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, autoregressive models — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: Why does a high sample correlation between two price levels fail to establish a tradable mean-reverting spread?
Answer: Correlation does not establish stationarity of the hedged residual.
Source: Engle & Granger, Co-integration and Error Correction, equilibrium errors and error correction — https://doi.org/10.2307/1913236

Question: A return series has little linear autocorrelation but its squared returns cluster. What feature is predictable in principle?
Answer: Conditional variance.
Source: Engle, Risk and Volatility, conditional heteroskedasticity and volatility forecasting — https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/06/engle-lecture.pdf

Question: A sample has dependence over weeks but the bootstrap uses two-day blocks. Which uncertainty can it understate?
Answer: Sampling uncertainty attributable to dependence beyond two days.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, bootstrapping and time series — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: What is average dollar P&L per trade in this sample?
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, expected return and return distributions — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: Starting at 100 independent observations, how many total observations would halve the charted standard error?
Explanation: Halving standard error requires four times the independent observations.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, parameter estimation and sample moments — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: What beta is implied by the plotted fitted line?
Explanation: A 4-point market move changes the fit by 6 points.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, time series regression and fitted values — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: What correlation between A and B does this matrix imply?
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, covariance matrices and portfolio variance — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: What is the first difference at date 4?
Answer: +3 index points.
Explanation: Subtract date 3's level from date 4's level.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, stationarity and differencing — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: What is the half-life of the plotted expected deviation?
Answer: One step.
Explanation: Every step halves its distance from zero.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, autoregressive models — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: For spread A − 2B, what is the residual at the fourth observation?
Explanation: 27 − 2 × 13. A short example alone cannot establish stationarity.
Source: Engle & Granger, Co-integration and Error Correction, equilibrium errors and error correction — https://doi.org/10.2307/1913236

Question: Which observation contributes the largest news term to a GARCH update with positive shock coefficient?
Answer: Day 2.
Explanation: Its squared residual is 16.
Source: Engle, Risk and Volatility, conditional heteroskedasticity and volatility forecasting — https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/06/engle-lecture.pdf

Question: Which resample preserves two contiguous three-day blocks?
Answer: A.
Explanation: Days 4–6 and 1–3 remain adjacent within their blocks.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, bootstrapping and time series — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: Which fitted stock is more sensitive to the market even though it has a lower intercept?
Answer: B.
Explanation: B gains four points for a two-point market move. A gains one.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, time series regression and fitted values — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: Read the two diagonal entries. What volatility product belongs in the denominator of the correlation formula?
Explanation: √0.09 × √0.04 = 0.30 × 0.20. Both returns are expressed in decimals.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, covariance matrices and portfolio variance — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: Which residual path gives a stronger visual reason to investigate a break in the hedge relationship?
Answer: B.
Explanation: B shifts upward and stays displaced. The short plot motivates a stability test.
Source: Engle & Granger, Co-integration and Error Correction, equilibrium errors and error correction — https://doi.org/10.2307/1913236

Question: This forecast is in squared percentage points. What daily volatility corresponds to session C?
Explanation: Volatility is the square root of the forecast variance of 9.
Source: Engle, Risk and Volatility, conditional heteroskedasticity and volatility forecasting — https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/06/engle-lecture.pdf

Question: Which band gives a less precise estimate of the mean return?
Answer: The block-resampling band.
Explanation: It is 10 bp wide versus 4 bp for the IID band. Width in this example measures uncertainty.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, bootstrapping and time series — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: Before assessing a signal, what forecast needs to be specified so that a failure is observable?
Answer: An outcome, direction and horizon conditional on a defined signal.
Explanation: The high-pressure group earns −8 bp against +2 bp for its control. This observation runs against a forecast of a relative rebound over that window.
Source: QuantConnect, Research Guide, hypothesis-driven strategy research — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/key-concepts/research-guide

Question: A strategy decides after today's close and trades at tomorrow's open. Where should the realized holding-return label begin?
Answer: At the executable next open.
Explanation: The executable entry is 110 at the next open. Exiting at 121 earns 10% before costs. Using the earlier decision close of 100 would include a move before entry.
Source: QuantConnect, Research Guide, look-ahead bias and target construction — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/key-concepts/research-guide

Question: How do you standardize an observation using a known mean and standard deviation?
Answer: Subtract the mean and divide by the standard deviation.
Explanation: Clipping the scores to [−5, 5] caps the extremes at −5 and +5. Standardizing a score would instead center it on the mean and scale it by the standard deviation.
Source: scikit-learn, Common Pitfalls, data leakage and preprocessing — https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html

Question: What does a cross-sectional rank information coefficient compare at a formation date?
Answer: Ranks of eligible names' forecasts with ranks of their subsequent returns.
Explanation: C and D exchange ranks between forecast and outcome. That disagreement lowers the rank correlation below a perfect +1.
Source: Alphalens, factor_information_coefficient and cross-sectional Spearman rank correlation — https://github.com/quantopian/alphalens/blob/master/alphalens/performance.py

Question: What does a forecast-decay curve measure?
Answer: How predictive strength changes with the time between signal and outcome.
Explanation: At a one-second delay the 5 bp gross edge still covers 4 bp of costs. At two seconds only 3 bp of gross edge remains.
Source: Boyd et al., Multi-Period Trading via Convex Optimization, multi-period forecasts and trading costs — https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/cvx_portfolio.html

Question: What does cross-sectional sector demeaning subtract from each stock's score?
Answer: Its sector's mean score on that date.
Explanation: The bank scores of 8 and 4 average 6. Subtracting that bank mean leaves scores of +2 and −2.
Source: Avellaneda & Lee, Statistical Arbitrage in the U.S. Equities Market, factor models and residual returns — https://math.nyu.edu/inmemoriam/avellaneda/AvellanedaLeeStatArb20090616.pdf

Question: Why can two profitable signals contribute little diversification when combined?
Answer: They can forecast or hold nearly the same exposures.
Explanation: A and B have correlation 0.98, so blending them may retain much the same exposure. C has correlation 0.12 with A.
Source: Boyd et al., Multi-Period Trading via Convex Optimization, forecasts and combined portfolio objectives — https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/cvx_portfolio.html

Question: What does effective breadth count in a systematic strategy?
Answer: Approximately independent forecasting or risk opportunities.
Explanation: A and B have identical factor loadings. Counting both positions as independent bets would overstate breadth.
Source: CFA Institute, Analysis of Active Portfolio Management, skill and breadth — https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/analysis-active-portfolio-management

Question: At one formation date, what is ranked on the outcome side of a rank IC calculation?
Answer: Each asset’s subsequent return over the forecast horizon.
Explanation: Use the same asset universe as the forecasts.
Source: Alphalens, factor_information_coefficient and cross-sectional Spearman rank correlation — https://github.com/quantopian/alphalens/blob/master/alphalens/performance.py

Question: Rank stocks by larger score. Which stock has the largest absolute change from forecast rank to realized rank?
Answer: C.
Explanation: C goes from last in the forecast to first by realized return, moving two places.
Source: Alphalens, factor_information_coefficient and cross-sectional Spearman rank correlation — https://github.com/quantopian/alphalens/blob/master/alphalens/performance.py

Question: Every forecast score is transformed by the same strictly increasing function. What happens to Spearman IC?
Answer: It stays the same.
Explanation: The transformation preserves the rankings.
Source: Alphalens, factor_information_coefficient and cross-sectional Spearman rank correlation — https://github.com/quantopian/alphalens/blob/master/alphalens/performance.py

Question: A liquidity-demand hypothesis predicts reversal after forced selling. What direction of subsequent residual return would challenge the prediction?
Answer: Continued negative residual returns in that prespecified window.
Source: QuantConnect, Research Guide, hypothesis-driven strategy research — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/key-concepts/research-guide

Question: An overnight jump occurs before a next-open entry. Should that jump enter this trade's holding return?
Answer: No. It occurs before the position exists.
Source: QuantConnect, Research Guide, look-ahead bias and target construction — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/key-concepts/research-guide

Question: A feature uses a trailing mean of 4 and standard deviation of 2. A new value is 7. What is its z-score?
Source: scikit-learn, Common Pitfalls, data leakage and preprocessing — https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html

Question: If every forecast rank is correct in reverse order with no ties, what is the Spearman IC?
Explanation: Worked example — Each step up the forecast ranking goes with one step down the outcome ranking, so rank correlation is −1.
Source: Alphalens, factor_information_coefficient and cross-sectional Spearman rank correlation — https://github.com/quantopian/alphalens/blob/master/alphalens/performance.py

Question: A signal's expected gross edge falls below the round-trip cost before an order can arrive. What is the implication for that implementation?
Answer: Its expected executable net edge is negative.
Source: Boyd et al., Multi-Period Trading via Convex Optimization, multi-period forecasts and trading costs — https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/cvx_portfolio.html

Question: A stock scores 7 while its sector mean is 5. What sector-relative score remains?
Source: Avellaneda & Lee, Statistical Arbitrage in the U.S. Equities Market, factor models and residual returns — https://math.nyu.edu/inmemoriam/avellaneda/AvellanedaLeeStatArb20090616.pdf

Question: A 60/40 forecast blend combines +10 bp and −5 bp estimates on the same horizon. What is its forecast?
Answer: +4 bp.
Explanation: 0.6 × 10 + 0.4 × (−5). Worked example — The 60% sleeve contributes 6 bp. The 40% sleeve subtracts 2 bp.
Source: Boyd et al., Multi-Period Trading via Convex Optimization, forecasts and combined portfolio objectives — https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/cvx_portfolio.html

Question: Ten equity trades all load on one earnings surprise. Why is ten a poor estimate of independent breadth?
Answer: The shared driver makes the bets dependent.
Source: CFA Institute, Analysis of Active Portfolio Management, skill and breadth — https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/analysis-active-portfolio-management

Question: A researcher changes the intended holding period after inspecting the results. What evidence is needed to test the revised hypothesis independently?
Answer: Outcomes from a fresh untouched period or sample.
Source: QuantConnect, Research Guide, hypothesis-driven strategy research — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/key-concepts/research-guide

Question: A label depends on a five-day exit. When is its realized value first available for model training?
Answer: After the exit observation and any required publication delay.
Source: QuantConnect, Research Guide, look-ahead bias and target construction — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/key-concepts/research-guide

Question: Why must a time-series scaler fitted for a test fold exclude later observations?
Answer: Future distribution information would leak into the feature.
Source: scikit-learn, Common Pitfalls, data leakage and preprocessing — https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html

Question: Why can a positive cross-sectional IC coexist with a losing long-only portfolio?
Answer: Relative rankings can be correct while the entire market falls.
Source: Alphalens, factor_information_coefficient and cross-sectional Spearman rank correlation — https://github.com/quantopian/alphalens/blob/master/alphalens/performance.py

Question: Why can holding longer improve net results even when the short-horizon gross forecast is stronger?
Answer: Less frequent trading may save more cost than the lost gross edge.
Source: Boyd et al., Multi-Period Trading via Convex Optimization, multi-period forecasts and trading costs — https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/cvx_portfolio.html

Question: A sector-neutral score still loads strongly on market beta. What did the sector adjustment fail to control?
Answer: Within-sector exposure to beta.
Source: Avellaneda & Lee, Statistical Arbitrage in the U.S. Equities Market, factor models and residual returns — https://math.nyu.edu/inmemoriam/avellaneda/AvellanedaLeeStatArb20090616.pdf

Question: A signal works alone. What comparison tests its incremental value in an existing stack?
Answer: Compare the existing model with and without the signal on the same held-out dates and costs.
Source: Boyd et al., Multi-Period Trading via Convex Optimization, forecasts and combined portfolio objectives — https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/cvx_portfolio.html

Question: Under the simplified information-ratio relation with fixed skill and independent bets, how does quadrupling breadth affect the predicted information ratio?
Answer: It doubles.
Explanation: The relation scales with the square root of breadth.
Source: CFA Institute, Analysis of Active Portfolio Management, skill and breadth — https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/analysis-active-portfolio-management

Question: By how many basis points did the high-pressure group underperform its control?
Answer: 10 bp.
Explanation: −8 minus +2 is −10 bp, opposite a relative rebound in this sample.
Source: QuantConnect, Research Guide, hypothesis-driven strategy research — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/key-concepts/research-guide

Question: For entry at next open and exit as marked, what is the tradable holding return before costs?

Question: If the rule clips raw scores to [−5, 5], which pair of values do A and D receive?
Explanation: Clipping caps magnitudes without dropping the names.
Source: scikit-learn, Common Pitfalls, data leakage and preprocessing — https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html

Question: Which pair of securities reverses order between forecast and outcome?
Answer: C and D.
Explanation: A and B keep their ranks.
Source: Alphalens, factor_information_coefficient and cross-sectional Spearman rank correlation — https://github.com/quantopian/alphalens/blob/master/alphalens/performance.py

Question: With a 4 bp all-in cost, what is the latest plotted delay with positive expected net edge?
Answer: 1 second.
Explanation: 5 − 4 is positive; 3 − 4 is negative.
Source: Boyd et al., Multi-Period Trading via Convex Optimization, multi-period forecasts and trading costs — https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/cvx_portfolio.html

Question: Which stock has the highest score after subtracting its own sector mean?
Answer: The first bank.
Explanation: Residual scores are +2, −2, +1 and −1.
Source: Avellaneda & Lee, Statistical Arbitrage in the U.S. Equities Market, factor models and residual returns — https://math.nyu.edu/inmemoriam/avellaneda/AvellanedaLeeStatArb20090616.pdf

Question: Based only on this matrix, which signal is least redundant with A?
Answer: C.
Explanation: Its correlation with A is 0.12 versus B's 0.98; predictive quality is a separate question.
Source: Boyd et al., Multi-Period Trading via Convex Optimization, forecasts and combined portfolio objectives — https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/cvx_portfolio.html

Question: Combining which two positions duplicates the same factor bet in this chart?
Answer: A and B.
Explanation: They have identical factor loadings.
Source: CFA Institute, Analysis of Active Portfolio Management, skill and breadth — https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/analysis-active-portfolio-management

Question: Compare the daily rank ICs. What is their equally weighted mean across formation dates?
Answer: Zero.
Explanation: The +1 and −1 cancel, and the middle date contributes zero.
Source: Alphalens, factor_information_coefficient and cross-sectional Spearman rank correlation — https://github.com/quantopian/alphalens/blob/master/alphalens/performance.py

Question: What determines a winner in cross-sectional momentum?
Answer: Its past return relative to other eligible assets over the specified window.
Explanation: All four stocks lost money. B ranks first because its −2% return is the least negative of the four.
Source: Kenneth French Data Library, portfolio construction descriptions, momentum factor and portfolios formed on prior returns — https://mba.tuck.dartmouth.edu/pages/faculty/ken.french/data_library.html

Question: What input determines direction in a simple sign-based time-series momentum rule?
Answer: The asset's own trailing excess return.
Explanation: The price slips from 112 to 105 but remains above its starting level of 100. With zero cash return, the two-period signal is still positive.
Source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen, Time Series Momentum, past excess return sign and volatility scaling — https://www.aqr.com/Insights/Research/Journal-Article/Time-Series-Momentum

Question: For positive book equity, which direction of book-to-market indicates cheaper equity per dollar of book value?
Answer: Higher book-to-market.
Explanation: B has $60m of book value against $100m of market capitalization, a book-to-market ratio of 0.60.
Source: Kenneth French Data Library, portfolio construction descriptions, book-to-market portfolios and HML construction — https://mba.tuck.dartmouth.edu/pages/faculty/ken.french/data_library.html

Question: What economic characteristics commonly enter a composite quality signal?
Answer: Measures of profitability, growth and safety.
Explanation: For B, profitability and safety each score 1. For A, the +2 profitability score is offset by a −2 safety score in the equal-weight average.
Source: Asness, Frazzini & Pedersen, Quality Minus Junk, profitability, growth and safety dimensions — https://www.aqr.com/insights/research/working-paper/quality-minus-junk

Question: What does a carry estimate hold fixed when isolating the return from holding an instrument?
Answer: The specified valuation or market conditions, apart from passage of time.
Explanation: The +25 bp carry contribution is outweighed by −40 bp of spot repricing and −3 bp of costs, leaving −18 bp overall.
Source: Koijen et al., Carry, asset-class definitions and carry versus price changes — https://www.aqr.com/Insights/Research/Journal-Article/Carry

Question: What price behavior does a short-horizon reversal signal hypothesize after temporary selling pressure?
Answer: A subsequent rebound toward a reference level.
Explanation: Trades alternate between 99 and 101 while the midpoint stays at 100. Bid–ask bounce can mimic reversals in transaction prices.
Source: Avellaneda & Lee, Statistical Arbitrage in the U.S. Equities Market, mean-reverting residual strategies — https://math.nyu.edu/inmemoriam/avellaneda/AvellanedaLeeStatArb20090616.pdf

Question: A pairs residual A − βB is unusually high and expected to revert. What is the basic spread direction?
Answer: Short the residual: sell A and buy β units of B per unit of A, for positive β.
Explanation: The spread crosses the +2 entry threshold in session 3. The short spread is held until the reading falls below +0.5 in session 5.
Source: Avellaneda & Lee, Statistical Arbitrage in the U.S. Equities Market, hedge construction and residual trading signals — https://math.nyu.edu/inmemoriam/avellaneda/AvellanedaLeeStatArb20090616.pdf

Question: How is abnormal return defined in an event study?
Answer: Observed return less the return predicted by the specified normal-return model.
Explanation: On day 0, the asset’s 6% return exceeds the modeled 2% return by four points. Day +1 adds one more point of abnormal return.
Source: MacKinlay, Event Studies in Economics and Finance, event windows, normal returns and abnormal returns — https://www.bu.edu/econ/files/2011/01/MacKinlay-1996-Event-Studies-in-Economics-and-Finance.pdf

Question: What constitutes an independent repetition of a month-of-year seasonal pattern more closely than another day in that month?
Answer: Another year containing the same calendar phase.
Explanation: Subtracting other-day returns from month-end returns gives +7 bp in discovery and −2 bp in the holdout. The seasonal premium changes sign.
Source: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3e, seasonal patterns and time series cross-validation — https://otexts.com/fpp3/

Question: How does a positive inventory position affect the reservation price in a basic inventory-averse dealer model?
Answer: It lowers the dealer's reservation price relative to the midpoint.

Question: What makes a feasible portfolio mean–variance dominated?
Answer: Another feasible portfolio offers at least as much expected return with no more variance and a strict improvement in one.

Question: What is covariance shrinkage toward a target?
Answer: A weighted blend of the sample covariance matrix with a structured target.
Explanation: A 50–50 blend of a sample estimate of 8 and a target of 2 gives 5. The estimate moves halfway toward the target.

Question: What is the feasible set of a constrained portfolio problem?
Answer: All portfolios satisfying the specified constraints simultaneously.
Explanation: Position A starts at 40% against a 35% cap. Cutting at least five percentage points brings it within the limit.
Source: Cvxportfolio, Constraints, long-only, leverage, factor and turnover constraints — https://www.cvxportfolio.com/en/stable/constraints.html

Question: How is gross exposure computed from signed portfolio weights?
Answer: Sum their absolute values.
Explanation: The 70% short counts toward gross exposure by its magnitude. Adding it to longs of 60% and 40% gives 170% gross.

Question: What converts an asset's marginal contribution to portfolio volatility into its component contribution?
Answer: Multiply the volatility derivative by that asset's portfolio weight.
Explanation: The equity sleeve contributes 6 of the 10 total volatility points. Its share of portfolio risk is 60%.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, risk budgeting portfolios and Euler decomposition — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: Under linear scaling, what multiplier takes unscaled volatility to a target?
Answer: Target volatility divided by estimated unscaled volatility.
Explanation: At 8% forecast volatility, a 12% target calls for 1.5× exposure. The leverage cap limits the actual multiplier to 1.25×.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, portfolio risk, leverage and volatility-based sizing — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: What objective does the classical Kelly fraction maximize under its probability model?
Answer: Expected logarithmic wealth growth.
Explanation: The 20% stake has the highest estimated log growth among the plotted stakes. The 30% stake puts more wealth at risk and yields lower estimated log growth.
Source: Busseti, Ryu & Boyd, Risk-Constrained Kelly Gambling, Kelly objective and drawdown constraints — https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.06183

Question: What defines a no-trade region around a target allocation?

Explanation: The weight reaches 54% on Wednesday, the first observation outside the 47–53% band.

Question: In receding-horizon portfolio optimization, which planned trade is sent now?
Answer: Only the first trade; later trades are replanned with new information.
Explanation: The fast plan earns 7 bp and then loses 6 bp. The gradual plan earns 4 bp and then 2 bp, giving it the higher two-period total.

Question: A covariance estimate puts 30% weight on the target. What weight remains on the sample estimate?
Explanation: The two convex weights sum to one.

Question: A sleeve has weight 0.25 and marginal contribution to volatility 8 percentage points per unit of weight. What is its component contribution?

Explanation: Multiply weight by marginal volatility.
Source: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application, risk budgeting portfolios and Euler decomposition — https://portfoliooptimizationbook.com/book/

Question: For a repeatable even-money bet with known win probability 50%, what fraction maximizes expected log growth?

Explanation: At fair odds there is no edge to compensate for risk.

Question: The target is above the sample estimate. Which direction does positive shrinkage move the covariance?

Question: Using additive component contributions, what is total portfolio volatility?
Answer: 8 percentage points.
Explanation: The hedge contributes −1, so 6 + 3 − 1 = 8.

Question: The plotted outcomes follow the same win and loss. Which fraction ends with the most wealth among the three shown?

Question: With 100% weight on a diagonal shrinkage target, what happens to off-diagonal sample covariances?

Question: What does a negative marginal contribution to volatility mean for a small increase in that position with other positions fixed?

Question: Two models run on identical days. Which bootstrap design preserves the pairing when comparing them?
Answer: Resample matched time blocks of their joint daily results.

Question: A small-cap value strategy beats a large-cap growth index. Which attribution concern arises first?
Answer: Style and size exposure differences may explain the comparison.
Source: CFA Institute, Portfolio Performance Evaluation, benchmark selection and appraisal — https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/portfolio-performance-evaluation

Question: A paper target book matches the research signal but live trades miss many fills. Which stage should be examined before retraining the model?
Answer: Order execution and fill reconciliation.
Source: QuantConnect, Live Reconciliation, comparing backtest, paper and live performance — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/research-environment/meta-analysis/live-reconciliation

Question: Why might a client's money-weighted return lag a manager's time-weighted return?
Answer: The client invested more capital before poor subperiod performance.
Source: CFA Institute, Portfolio Performance Evaluation, time-weighted and money-weighted returns — https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/portfolio-performance-evaluation

Question: Why can multiplying daily Sharpe by √252 misstate annual Sharpe?
Answer: Serial dependence changes the variance of aggregated returns.
Source: CFA Institute, Portfolio Performance Evaluation, risk-adjusted performance measures — https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/portfolio-performance-evaluation

Question: A portfolio has a low tracking error to cash but a high one to an equity benchmark. What changed?
Answer: The reference return series used to define active risk.
Source: CFA Institute, Analysis of Active Portfolio Management, active risk and information ratio — https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/analysis-active-portfolio-management

Question: A residual labeled stock-selection alpha disappears after adding a missing style factor. What did it previously include?
Answer: Return associated with the omitted factor exposure.

Question: Why can applying a per-dollar-traded fee to half-sum turnover understate cost?
Answer: Half-sum turnover counts only one side of a balanced rebalance.
Source: Cvxportfolio, Cost Models, trade notional and transaction cost models — https://www.cvxportfolio.com/en/stable/costs.html

Question: An interval for a single chosen winner ignores the search across many alternatives. What source of uncertainty is missing?
Answer: Strategy selection or multiple-testing effects.
Source: Bailey et al., The Probability of Backtest Overfitting, sampling uncertainty and selection of winners — https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/backtest-prob.pdf

Question: Why establish the benchmark before observing performance?
Answer: Choosing one afterward can make an ordinary result appear unusually strong.
Source: CFA Institute, Portfolio Performance Evaluation, benchmark selection and appraisal — https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/portfolio-performance-evaluation

Question: Why attribute returns to the positions actually held at each time?
Answer: Targets can differ from filled exposures, distorting reconstructed P&L.
Source: QuantConnect, Live Reconciliation, comparing backtest, paper and live performance — https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/research-environment/meta-analysis/live-reconciliation

Question: What is the return during the second investment subperiod alone?
Explanation: 210/200 − 1. The 90 deposit is external cash.
Source: CFA Institute, Portfolio Performance Evaluation, time-weighted and money-weighted returns — https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/portfolio-performance-evaluation

Question: Which strategy has the higher monthly Sharpe?
Answer: A.
Source: CFA Institute, Portfolio Performance Evaluation, risk-adjusted performance measures — https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/portfolio-performance-evaluation

Question: What is the sample standard deviation of the three monthly active returns?
Answer: Zero.
Explanation: All active returns are +1 percentage point; a finite information ratio cannot be computed.
Source: CFA Institute, Analysis of Active Portfolio Management, active risk and information ratio — https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/analysis-active-portfolio-management

Question: Under Brinson–Fachler, what is the tech allocation contribution in percentage points?
Answer: +0.4 percentage points.
Explanation: 0.10 × 4 percentage points.
Source: CFA Institute, Portfolio Performance Evaluation, return attribution and Brinson frameworks — https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/portfolio-performance-evaluation

Question: What is one-way turnover under the half-sum convention?
